data.name: Ayanaj
data.gender_notes: Ayanaj is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Ayanaj is a name derived from the Sanskrit language, which means 'radiant', 'shining forward'. This name is associated with the god Ayan, who represents the rising sun and the dawn of a new day. Ayanaj is a powerful and auspicious name, filled with the promise of a bright and successful future. The name Ayanaj carries the meaning “Radiant, Shining Forward” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Ayanaj usually hope their child will grow to embody radiant, shining forward and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Embrace the light and radiance within.

Letting the name Ayanaj continue to carry this rich symbolism could inspire those named with the name to embody these qualities - to bring light and sunshine to those around them.

historical_references.reference: The name Ayanaj is mentioned in the Mahabharata, an ancient Indian epic poem. It is the name of a king who ruled over the Anga country in the eastern part of India. The Mahabharata was likely composed between 400 BCE and 200 CE.
historical_references.context: Ancient Indian epic poem, Mahabharata, mentions Ayanaj as a king of Anga country.

historical_references.reference: Ayanaj is also mentioned in the Puranas, a set of ancient Indian texts. He is described as a king of Magadha, a kingdom located in the eastern part of India. The Puranas were likely composed between 400 CE and 1200 CE.
